cause: The full gate encountered the macOS sandbox-exec policy, and two gate processes were started concurrently during this session, producing golden-test drift.
impact: The repository-wide gate cannot be declared green in this environment; the v1.8.2 statistical-exploration focused suites remain green.
lesson: Run the full gate exactly once and serially in an environment that permits sandbox-exec before release acceptance.

cause: Browser smoke showed that the raw dataset stage has no payload_ref even though its raw_data artifact is present under raw_snapshot, while the shared source resolver required payload_ref.
impact: Raw Data statistical exploration and existing source-bound column context were blocked in the visible UI.
lesson: Every source-stage browser journey must exercise raw nodes whose payload_ref is intentionally null and resolve the authoritative raw_data artifact by typed artifact metadata.

cause: Browser smoke reached grouped summarize confirmation and the XLSX exporter received nested filter and variable mappings instead of scalar cells.
impact: A valid grouped exploration preview could not be saved as the required durable HTML/PDF/XLSX artifact set.
lesson: Export adapters must normalize every nested result field to an inspectable scalar representation before writing spreadsheet cells.

cause: Grouped summarize output needed a durable Table projection instead of a detail-drawer payload.
impact: The right panel stays compact while the complete grouped statistical result is readable in Table.
lesson: Keep large grouped statistical outputs in the result table and leave the source-node panel focused on controls and a compact preview.

cause: The expanded variable picker still used visually heavy checkbox rows after the first compact disclosure pass.
impact: The expanded list now uses a compact two-column grid with small native checkboxes, shorter rows, and visible type hints.
lesson: For dense variable selectors, compact grid density and restrained native control sizing are part of functional usability, not only visual polish.

cause: The OLS result already carried authoritative confidence bounds but the non-code Table surface did not expose them.
impact: The Table coefficient view now shows a numeric 95% confidence interval when authoritative bounds exist and a visible dash otherwise.
lesson: Expose authoritative model intervals in the primary no-code result table instead of asking users to calculate them.

cause: The post-preview OLS context still rendered predictor choices as large unstyled checkbox rows, which made a dense no-code selection surface visually heavy.
impact: The OLS context now keeps Outcome as a compact single-select row and presents predictors as small, two-column, multi-select options without changing request semantics.
lesson: Dense statistical variable choices should use compact, scannable controls with explicit grouping instead of default checkbox flow layout.

cause: Browser acceptance of the full Class 3 exercise showed four surfaces where the native no-code path could not produce the Stata result at all: the exploration-to-OLS handoff wrote no covariance and a genesis Draft carries no editable_schema, so HC1 was unreachable-to-change; adjusted R-squared was absent from every surface; the pooled correlation matrix reached Table and every export as an unlabelled nested array; and residual/fitted diagnostics plotted the bounded 500-row preview while titling it N=500 on a 4110-row model.
impact: The handoff now carries an explicit robust/unadjusted covariance into model_params and the exploration context identity; normalize emits r_squared_adj plus a bounded full residual/fitted vector; corr emits labelled pairs and a named square table consumed by Table, HTML, PDF and XLSX; diagnostic titles state N=total or 'first N of M'. Verified live: run_inputs.form.covariance='unadjusted' produces model_type 'ols' with se 3.2894 against the HC1 3.5207, adj R2 0.002748 renders in Table, the 18x18 matrix renders labelled, and residuals_vs_pblack.png reports N=4110.
lesson: A handoff that materializes a params-only Draft must collect every inference choice at the handoff, because no later surface can edit it; and a bounded preview must never be the source for a plot that is presented as the model's diagnostic.

cause: Commit 056782a added the class3 residual/fitted predictor plots to visualization.py without regenerating tests/golden, so four engine goldens (continuous_ols, count_poisson, panel, imputation) had been red since 2026-07-24 and the line's declared zero-drift gate was silently failing.
impact: The four goldens now carry the two intentional figure artifacts (fitted_vs_x, residuals_vs_x). Verified against a pristine HEAD checkout that the drift predated the Stata-parity work; the delta is additive only, with no artifact removed and no coefficient changed.
lesson: A commit that adds a new run artifact must regenerate the engine goldens in the same change, otherwise the drift guard degrades into a permanently red test that hides later real drift.

cause: The first independent import of the new workflow runtime exposed a circular import in the exploration log storage dependency, and the structural context guard also caught a direct compiler-owned artifact-index string in the Agent runtime.
impact: Independent log import and the full structural guard were temporarily red; no workflow artifact was accepted from the affected path.
lesson: New Agent workflow adapters must be independently importable and must use repository-owned artifact accessors instead of reading compiler-owned sources directly.

cause: The full backend gate completed with 3526 passed, 8 skipped, and 1 xfailed, while 23 remaining failures were caused by macOS sandbox-exec permission denial and temporary fixture repositories without a local .venv; golden checks and all frontend tests passed, and TypeScript typecheck passed.
impact: The release gate is not globally green in this managed environment; workflow-specific and sandbox-independent suites remain green, but a full release claim is not made.
lesson: Keep environment-blocked sandbox evidence separate from the native statistical workflow acceptance evidence, and do not claim the full gate passed when only product slices are green.

cause: A real Agent confirmation reached the Class 3 workflow with a graph node hash in target artifact_id; source ownership validation rejected the executable proposal with HTTP 500.
impact: The first post-restart browser confirmation did not execute the workflow; no statistical artifacts were produced by that attempt.
lesson: Every Agent-facing workflow proposal must canonicalize the durable source artifact identity before confirmation, not only at execution.

cause: Backend regression ran 3573 passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed with zero failures outside two environment-blocked suites; both reference exercises were driven end to end against a live DeepSeek-backed agent on freshly created projects.
impact: Agent-composed workflows now express categorical dummy expansion and polynomial powers. Exercise 1 completed 10/10 steps with coefficients matching an independent statsmodels computation; Exercise 2 reproduced the assignment's published pblack coefficients (-10.407611, 5.927226, 6.486635, 8.041094) exactly. Derived terms are expanded by one module shared by the proposal validator and the executor, so validation cannot drift from construction, and a branch carrying derived terms materializes a content-addressed augmented upload while the original upload stays byte-identical. test_gate_script.py and test_devline_enforcement.py stayed blocked by a vite dev server this session did not start, so no global release claim is made.
lesson: A completed step that silently answered a different question is worse than a failed one. summarize_detail ignored group_by and returned one pooled summary for a per-year request; model.genesis accepted a categorical code column as a linear predictor. Both produced plausible numbers under a green status, and only a comparison against known answers exposed them.

cause: The multi-step workflow was first built to answer a single course exercise and that exercise was encoded in the server: a named preset whose bindings were its variables, a fixed set of its survey years, a diagnostics gate keyed to its column names, a UI placeholder suggesting those years, and a report line naming it to every future user.
impact: The preset compile path and its bindings were deleted, leaving an Agent-composed step list as the only accepted form. 98 exercise-specific references were removed from product code; two documented legacy-compat reads remain so drafts created before the rename still resume. Two step operations that a composed plan could name but the registry never declared are now registered, so the registry is again the closed set it claims to be. Backend 3591 passed, frontend 1419 passed, tsc clean; both reference exercises re-verified live with unchanged coefficients.
lesson: Tests of the exercise cannot catch the exercise being encoded, because the encoding is what they assert. A guard that scans product source for a specific assignment's identifiers is the check that does catch it; it must treat underscore as a boundary, since the real defect took the shape residuals_vs_<column>.
